short: Thailand has no AI law. ETDA and the digital ministry held a public hearing on the draft principles of an AI law from 11 to 24 June 2025; the Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 binds, with administrative fines of up to 5 million baht.
title: Thailand AI Laws
subtitle: A draft AI law at the principles stage, and the PDPA that binds
body_html:
Status at a glance

Draft AI law, not yet before parliament. Thailand has no AI law. The Electronic Transactions Development Agency (ETDA), with the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society, put the draft principles of an AI law ((ร่าง) หลักการของกฎหมายว่าด้วยปัญญาประดิษฐ์) to public hearing from 11 to 24 June 2025. The draft is risk-based, concentrates on high-risk uses, and would work through sector regulators, with provisions on sandboxes and text and data mining. The binding layer is the Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019). Verified on 25 October 2026 against ETDA and the Act's gazette text as the digital ministry publishes it.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberPublishedIn force
Draft principles of an AI lawETDA public hearing draft11 June 2025; comments to 24 June 2025No
Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562Royal Gazette, vol. 136, part 69 Kor, 27 May 201927 May 2019In force

Who regulates and enforces

  • ETDA: drafted the AI law principles.
  • Office of the Personal Data Protection Committee: the PDPA, through its expert committee (s. 90).

Scope and reach

The PDPA applies to controllers and processors in Thailand, whether the processing happens inside or outside the Kingdom, and to foreign controllers and processors that offer goods or services to, or monitor the behaviour of, people in Thailand (s. 5); a foreign controller must appoint a representative in Thailand (s. 37(5)).

Core obligations

  • Today: the PDPA's duties, including the stricter rules on sensitive data (s. 26).
  • Under the draft, if enacted: duties for high-risk AI uses, set through the sector regulators.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Breaches involving sensitive data under s. 26An administrative fine of up to THB 5,000,000PDPA s. 84Expert committee
General breaches by a controllerAn administrative fine of up to THB 3,000,000PDPA s. 83Expert committee
Criminal offencesUp to 1 year's imprisonment, a fine of up to THB 1,000,000, or bothPDPA s. 79Courts

What is coming next

  • A draft AI bill following the 2025 hearing; a report of a further draft heard in July 2026 could not be confirmed on an official source.

The July 2026 draft, as reported

ETDA published a revised draft Act on Artificial Intelligence in July 2026 for a hearing of about thirty days, closing on 14 August 2026. Law firms Tilleke & Gibbins, Rajah & Tann and Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer, which this site could read where ETDA's own hearing portal could not, give the release date as 2 July 2026 (Tilleke, HSF Kramer) or 9 July 2026 (Rajah & Tann); the discrepancy is not resolved here. The draft follows the 2025 principles but adds teeth. It applies to AI development or deployment that affects people in Thailand even when the act occurs abroad, and requires offshore providers of high-risk AI to appoint a local representative. It sorts systems into prohibited, high-risk and other AI, with duties concentrated on the high-risk tier and the list adjustable by royal decree. It introduces strict liability for damage caused by AI, labelling duties for AI-generated content, a sandbox for regulated sectors, data-sharing through the Big Data Institute, and a power for the AI committee to require in-country processing for services of national importance. Administrative fines run from THB 1 million to THB 5 million, and the regulator may ask a court to order ISPs to block a non-compliant system.

The draft keeps ETDA's AI Governance Center as the implementing body rather than creating a new regulator, and lets it issue cease orders jointly with sector regulators. After the hearing ETDA consults the ministries, then the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society sends the text to Cabinet for approval in principle before it enters the ordinary legislative process, so the earliest a binding act could pass is 2027. Thailand's neighbour Vietnam enacted a risk-based AI law in 2025, which the Thai drafters cite as regional precedent.

Until then the PDPA is the enforcement reality. The Personal Data Protection Committee announced on 1 August 2025 that it had issued eight administrative fines under the Act, its first, and in 2026 it has run consultations on guidance including a draft on data protection officers presented on 7 July 2026. A ministerial regulation on prevention of technology crimes was gazetted on 14 May 2026, and an August 2026 Prime Minister's Office regulation created a Data Center Business Policy Committee, both of which touch AI deployments at the edges.

Last verified

4 November 2026, against the sources above. The July 2026 draft is described from three law-firm reports, not from ETDA's hearing text, and is reported rather than verified; its release date differs between them. Left out: a party bill on AI, not confirmed on an official source.
